findings.text: blocking: report_carries_review_lines is not a plan-report-only reader — it is the shared admission guard called by both delivered_report_record (plan_review.py:2145) and _code_review_record (plan_review.py:2192). Switching its loop to _plan_report_lines strips a list marker for the health/code grammar too, but parse_health_review and _health_records still read _review_text_lines (review.py:1506), so guard and parser now disagree on a code report. A code review whose RUBRIC and FINDING lines are bulleted and whose TREATMENT line is bare passes the guard on a stripped bullet, then yields only the TREATMENT record, so parse_health_review returns zero items and zero findings and _code_review_record stores a review with every item absent — the composed-but-undelivered false-pass the guard exists to prevent, and previously the same report was refused as 'carries no RUBRIC or FINDING line'. The plan (§40) fixed the reader for the plan report and left the health grammar alone; the fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/a-plan-is-reviewed-before-it-is-built/a-bulleted-finding-is-read.html:33 asserts 'the run-review and health-review grammars do not move', which this contradicts. The plan-report half needs a plan-report-scoped admission guard (or _health_records must use the same reader) so the two paths cannot diverge.

blocking: baseline_suite is not valid JSON — the key is written '"failure_count: 2, "failure_ids"' with the opening quote unterminated, so json.loads fails at char 1134 ('Expecting : delimiter'), and after_suite on line 23 is truncated to {"revision", "command"} only, carrying no exit_status, completed, failure_count or failure_ids at all. The done-when requires both baseline_suite and after_suite to record failure_ids in the form tests/<file>::<name>, and promotion reads its gate receipt from these fields. The gate logs themselves are complete and readable (base-gate.log '2 failed, 116 passed ... EXIT=1'; head-gate.log '118 passed ... EXIT=0'), so the delta is recoverable, but the record the node landed states it in an unparseable field and omits it in the other.

follow-on: _delivered_status marks a partial report incomplete only when plan_report_rubric_name(rubric) == 'plan_review' (the content rubric), so a design review delivered after this section with one of its brief's items missing stores as DEFAULT_STATUS 'ready' and still covers its units. §40 states the mark for 'a review delivered after this section lands whose report leaves out an item its own brief listed', narrowed to no rubric. The worker narrowed it deliberately and disclosed the deviation in the manifest evidence_inputs, the follow_ons field and the fragment (line 35), because taking the design rubric with it reddens five deliveries outside this node's write paths; the done-when exercises a content review throughout. The section's un-narrowed wording is therefore not met, and the remainder is a separate node that updates those five deliveries.
